title: The 5 Deepest Lakes on Earth, Ranked (#4 Is Hidden Under Ice)

scenes.text: The five deepest lakes on Earth, ranked. One of them is buried under miles of ice.

scenes.label: O'Higgins-San Martin · 836 m
scenes.text: Number five: Lake O'Higgins San Martin, shared by Chile and Argentina. Eight hundred thirty-six meters deep.

scenes.label: Lake Vostok · 900 m+
scenes.text: Number four: Lake Vostok, hidden under more than two miles of Antarctic ice. At least nine hundred meters deep.

scenes.label: Caspian Sea · 1,025 m
scenes.text: Number three: the Caspian Sea. It's called a sea, but it's a lake, a thousand and twenty-five meters deep.

scenes.label: Tanganyika · 1,470 m
scenes.text: Number two: Lake Tanganyika, the deepest lake in Africa. About fourteen hundred seventy meters down.

scenes.label: Baikal · 1,640 m
scenes.text: Number one: Lake Baikal in Russia. About sixteen hundred forty meters deep, holding a fifth of the planet's unfrozen fresh water.

description:
The five deepest lakes on Earth, ranked by maximum depth.
One is buried under miles of Antarctic ice, and number one holds about a fifth of the planet's unfrozen surface fresh water.
Which lake would you most want to see?
first_comment: Which lake would you dive into first? And what should we rank next?
